title: One bridge capability
description: Something the bridge does, will do, or is asked to do. Three independent axes describe where it stands: stage (how far it is built), evidence (how far it is proven in the game) and health (how well it works). Keep them separate: a merged capability can have no game evidence, and a proven one can regress.

id.description: Stable id, '<area>.<name>' in lower kebab case. Never reused; a retired capability keeps its id with stage 'retired'.

summary.description: One or two plain sentences: what it lets someone do, for a reader who doesn't know the code.

parent.description: The id of a broader capability this one is part of.

kind.description: sense: reads game state. verb: changes the game. service: infrastructure other capabilities use (pipe, recorder, supervisor). surface: what a person sees (in-game UI). tool: host-side tooling (runner, MCP, CLI). safety: guards and kill paths. research: an investigation, not a feature.

stage.description: How far it is built. requested: someone asked, not triaged. proposed: triaged, design not agreed. planned: agreed and queued. building: work in progress (branch named). built: done offline on a branch. merged: on main. released: in a published package. retired: removed or replaced (say by what in notes).

evidence.description: How far it is proven in the game. none. offline: unit or self-tests only. partial: seen working in game for some rows, others unrun or inconclusive. proven: every required row passed in game. regressed: proven once, now failing.

health.description: How well it works as far as anyone knows. unknown (never run), works, caveats (works, with known_issues or quirks a user must know), degraded (works badly), broken.

priority.description: P0: blocks a consumer or a session now. P1: next up. P2: queued. P3: someday. Say why in priority_reason when it is P0 or P1.

branch.description: While building or built: the branch it lives on.

since.description: The bridge version that first had it, e.g. 0.8.19.

changed_in.description: The bridge version of its last behaviour change.

depends_on.description: Capability ids it needs. The validator refuses cycles and unknown ids.

demand.description: Who wants it and why. Consumers write and maintain their own entries here (and only theirs); the owner never edits another consumer's entry except to mark it met.

level.description: blocking: the consumer is stopped without it. needs: required for a planned milestone. wants: valuable, not required.

ref.description: The consumer's own requirement id or document anchor, e.g. 'S7' or 'runtime-requirements.md#scene-execution'.

milestone.description: The consumer's milestone that needs it, e.g. 'M4'.

note.description: What exactly they need from it, in their words.

met.description: Set when the consumer agrees the need is met.

surface.description: Where it shows up, so readers can find it and the validator can cross-check it.

code.description: Repository paths relative to the bridge project.

verification.description: What proves it. rows: test-card rows with their latest verdicts. tests: offline test files.

session.description: The session that gave the verdict, e.g. 'borg-4'.

optional.description: True for a row the capability doesn't need to be proven (an optional variant); every other row must pass for evidence 'proven'.

limits.description: Hard limits a user must plan around (e.g. 'at most 5 XF actors').

quirks.description: Nuances and idiosyncrasies: behaviour that is correct but surprising.

ref.description: A ledger id (RB-…), findings file or commit.

unknowns.description: Open questions, and how to settle each.

settle_by.description: How: a test row, a research brief, reading source.

improvements.description: Ways it could be better, not yet planned.

docs.description: Links (repository-relative) to design, knowledge and test-card sections.

updated.description: Date of the last change to this entry; every change also gets a changelog line.
